Fix a four-dimensional smooth spacetime region $U\subseteq\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with a stated orientation, spin structure, boundary conditions, and unit system. A selected model specifies a continuous global symmetry group $H$, its action on the fields and observables, the nondynamical background connections, the field and jet domains, a regulator and measure or formal perturbative generating functional, and the admissible local counterterms. A background connection is nondynamical model data: it transforms under local changes of background trivialization but is not integrated over.

Let $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{bg},U}^{g,p}$ be the finite-jet horizontal $p$-forms of ghost number $g$ generated by the nondynamical background connections and their BRST ghost jets, without matter-field jets, and restrict the model’s nilpotent BRST differential $s$ and horizontal exterior derivative $d_H$ to this background subalgebra. An infinitesimal local anomaly representative is a local horizontal four-form $a_4\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{bg},U}^{1,4}$ such that $sa_4+d_Hb_3=0$ for some $b_3\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{bg},U}^{2,3}$. The **local perturbative ’t Hooft anomaly** of the specified global symmetry is the class $[a_4]$ in the relative cohomology $H^{1,4}(s\mid d_H)$ of this background subalgebra, with the quotient taken using exactly the model’s admissible four-dimensional background counterterms and total-derivative boundary convention. Its class is zero exactly when an admissible local counterterm removes the infinitesimal background variation modulo a boundary term.

Any prescribed noninvariance of the classical action or selected couplings is an explicit-symmetry-breaking insertion and is separated before assigning this quantum anomaly class. It is not, by itself, a measure anomaly. A claim of anomaly matching therefore assumes the stated classical symmetry, or carries such breaking insertions separately.

This definition applies to a global symmetry whose background is nondynamical. If the same local class concerns a field integrated over as a gauge redundancy, it is a local gauge anomaly, not a ’t Hooft anomaly; an uncancelled gauge anomaly obstructs the proposed gauging unless a separately specified cancellation mechanism is included. The definition addresses only infinitesimal transformations and makes no claim about large or disconnected transformations, determinant-line holonomy, torsion phases, or a physical continuum limit.

derivations.claim: By [A1], each kernel and cokernel is finite-dimensional, so each top exterior power in the Definition is a one-dimensional complex vector space. The explicit invertible-band transitions supply the smooth line even across kernel jumps; the stated spectral identities give the cut-independent Quillen norm, and [A1] supplies the smooth compatible connection. Their tensor product and dual are therefore a one-dimensional Hermitian line with the specified Quillen metric.

Gauge covariance of the Dirac operators intertwines kernel and cokernel unitarily, and the conjugate operators have the same spectrum, so the endpoint map preserves the specified Quillen metric. Parallel transport is unitary. Therefore $u_*^{-1}\circ\mathrm{PT}_{A_t}$ is a unitary automorphism of a one-dimensional complex line, hence multiplication by a unique scalar of modulus one. A change of unit vector in the fiber conjugates that scalar, which does not change it because $U(1)$ is abelian. Therefore $\operatorname{Hol}_{\gamma}(\mathcal L)$ is a well-defined element of $U(1)$. By [F1], the local anomaly interface does not classify determinant-line holonomy; this phase is defined here as separate global loop data, not as a consequence of [F1].

Tensor factors are kept in increasing cut order; parity is $\operatorname{ind}D^+\bmod2$ if graded lines are used.

For each cut, define the scalar function $\zeta_a(z)=\sum_{\lambda>a}\lambda^{-z}$ using the positive $Q^+$ eigenvalues with multiplicity and real $\log\lambda$. Admissibility requires convergence on an initial right half-plane, a specified meromorphic continuation to a connected domain reaching $z=0$, regularity there, and smooth parameter dependence of $\zeta'_a(0)$. The **Quillen squared norm** is $\|\ell\|_Q^2=\exp(-\zeta'_a(0))\|\ell_a\|_{L^2}^2$. Finite bands satisfy $\zeta_a-\zeta_b=\sum_{a<\lambda<b}\lambda^{-z}$ and $\|\ell_b\|_{L^2}^2=(\prod_{a<\lambda<b}\lambda)\|\ell_a\|_{L^2}^2$, which give cut independence of this norm. Project $\widetilde\nabla^\pm$ to the cut subbundles and their complements. They induce a connection $\nabla^a$ on $L_a$. derivations.claim: By [A1], $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{bulk}}(M,b|_M)$ is the dual of $\mathcal L_\partial(M,b|_M)$. Evaluation of a one-dimensional vector space against its dual is a well-defined nondegenerate pairing to $\mathbb C$, so the tensor of the two boundary values gives the stated scalar.

The endpoint gauge maps preserve the specified evaluations by the equivariance included in the line-duality data. Write them as $u_*^\partial$ and $u_*^{\mathrm{bulk}}$. Then the scalar comparing $\mathrm{ev}_1\circ(\mathrm{PT}^{\partial}_\gamma\otimes\mathrm{PT}^{\mathrm{bulk}}_\gamma)$ with $\mathrm{ev}_0$ equals the scalar of $\mathrm{ev}_0\circ(((u_*^\partial)^{-1}\circ\mathrm{PT}^{\partial}_\gamma)\otimes((u_*^{\mathrm{bulk}})^{-1}\circ\mathrm{PT}^{\mathrm{bulk}}_\gamma))$. The latter is multiplication by $\operatorname{Hol}_\gamma(\mathcal L_\partial)\operatorname{Hol}_\gamma(\mathcal L_{\mathrm{bulk}})$ because both lines are one-dimensional. Hence the displayed diagram commutes exactly when this product is $1$. This is a definition of the scoped inflow interface, not an existence theorem for a bulk. [F2] explicitly excludes determinant-line holonomy, so it does not derive this geometric cancellation criterion or identify a particular global phase.

A selected model specifies a continuous global symmetry group $H$, its action on the fields and observables, the nondynamical background connections, the field and jet domains, a regulator and measure or formal perturbative generating functional, and the admissible local counterterms. A background connection is nondynamical model data: it transforms under local changes of background trivialization but is not integrated over.

Let $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{bg},U}^{g,p}$ be the finite-jet horizontal $p$-forms of ghost number $g$ generated by the nondynamical background connections and their BRST ghost jets, without matter-field jets, and restrict the model’s nilpotent BRST differential $s$ and horizontal exterior derivative $d_H$ to this background subalgebra. Its class is zero exactly when an admissible local counterterm removes the infinitesimal background variation modulo a boundary term.

Any prescribed noninvariance of the classical action or selected couplings is an explicit-symmetry-breaking insertion and is separated before assigning this quantum anomaly class. It is not, by itself, a measure anomaly. A claim of anomaly matching therefore assumes the stated classical symmetry, or carries such breaking insertions separately.

This definition applies to a global symmetry whose background is nondynamical. If the same local class concerns a field integrated over as a gauge redundancy, it is a local gauge anomaly, not a ’t Hooft anomaly; an uncancelled gauge anomaly obstructs the proposed gauging unless a separately specified cancellation mechanism is included. The definition addresses only infinitesimal transformations and makes no claim about large or disconnected transformations, determinant-line holonomy, torsion phases, or a physical continuum limit.

A **finite groupoid** is a small category in which every morphism is invertible, with finitely many isomorphism classes and a finite automorphism group at every object. Write $\pi_0(\mathcal C)$ for its set of isomorphism classes. Its **groupoid cardinality** is

$$|\mathcal C|:=\sum_{[c]\in\pi_0(\mathcal C)}\frac{1}{|\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal C}(c)|}.$$

For an isomorphism-invariant function $f:\pi_0(\mathcal C)\to\mathbb C$, define

$$\int_{c\in\mathcal C} f(c):=\sum_{[c]\in\pi_0(\mathcal C)}\frac{f(c)}{|\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal C}(c)|}.$$

For finite groupoids $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$, a functor $p:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$, and an object $d$ of $\mathcal D$, its **homotopy fiber** $\mathcal C_d$ has objects $(c,\alpha)$ with $\alpha:p(c)\overset{\cong}{\longrightarrow}d$ and morphisms $u:(c,\alpha)\to(c',\alpha')$ satisfying $\alpha'\circ p(u)=\alpha$. Define pullback and pushforward of invariant functions by

$$(p^*g)([c])=g([p(c)]),\qquad (p_!f)([d])=\int_{(c,\alpha)\in\mathcal C_d} f([c]).$$

A span $\mathcal X\xleftarrow{a}\mathcal E\xrightarrow{b}\mathcal Y$ of finite groupoids therefore induces the linear map $b_!a^*$ on invariant functions.

This is a direct operator calculation for this explicit bundle, not an application of a general index formula.

([[def-banach-space]]) and let $T:X\to Y$ be a bounded linear operator
([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]). Then $T$ is a **Fredholm operator** when
all three of the following hold:

1. $\ker T$ is finite dimensional, that is, admits an ordered basis of finite
   length ([[def-linear-basis]], [[def-dimension]]);
2. $\operatorname{ran}T$ is a closed subspace of $Y$
   ([[def-linear-subspace]]);
3. the **cokernel** $\operatorname{coker}T:=Y/\operatorname{ran}T$ is finite
   dimensional ([[def-quotient-vector-space-coset-notation]],
   [[def-dimension]]).

Here the cokernel is the algebraic quotient vector space; it also carries the
quotient seminorm of [[def-quotient-seminorm]], which is a norm when the range
is closed ([[thm-quotient-seminorm-is-a-norm-iff-subspace-is-closed]]), but the dimension in clause 3 is the vector-space dimension of the
quotient and does not depend on that norm.

For a Fredholm operator $T$ the **index** of $T$ is the integer

$$\operatorname{ind}T:=\dim_{\mathbb F}\ker T-\dim_{\mathbb F}\operatorname{coker}T$$

Here subtraction is in $\mathbb Z$, not in $\mathbb N$: write $a=\dim_{\mathbb F}\ker T$ and $b=\dim_{\mathbb F}\operatorname{coker}T$ and identify a natural $n$ with $[(n,0)]$. Precisely,

$$\operatorname{ind}T=[(a,b)]=[(a,0)]+(-[(b,0)])\in\mathbb Z$$

**Two remarks on the definition.** The closedness of the range is listed
explicitly as a hypothesis of the definition rather than extracted from the
other clauses. And no property of the index is asserted here; additivity,
local constancy and invariance under compact perturbations are separate
theorems.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: For the fundamental $SU(2)$ representation $F_A$ is a traceless $2\times2$ matrix over the commuting algebra of even curvature forms. Cayley--Hamilton gives $F_A^2=-\det(F_A)I$, hence $\operatorname{tr}F_A=\operatorname{tr}F_A^3=0$. Thus the odd Chern-character components $\operatorname{ch}_1(E)$ and $\operatorname{ch}_3(E)$ vanish. The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.
